qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Phase nine. Fourier transform and the F F T. This is how every signal splits into waves.
Count the crests in one second. Five crests means five hertz.
Count the waves in one second.
Add a faster, weaker wave of twelve hertz, and the sum is one wiggle.
Two waves added make one wiggle.
Each bar shows which wave is inside, and how strong.
Each bar: which wave, and how strong.
One signal, described over time and by frequency.
One signal, two descriptions.
Our target is a square wave, with sharp corners.
Target: a square wave.
Start with one smooth sine wave.
Start with one sine wave.
Add a wave three times as fast, and a third as strong.
Add a weaker wave, 3 times faster.
Then one five times as fast, and weaker still.
Then 5 times faster, weaker still.
Keep adding more waves, and the sum gets closer to the square, with sharper corners.
Keep adding: the corners sharpen.
A square wave needs only the odd waves, one, three, five, and so on.
A square wave needs only odd waves.
To find a bar, take eight samples of the wave.
To find the bars, take 8 samples.
A test arrow spins, and each sample scales it.
Each sample scales a spinning arrow.
A sample of zero makes no arrow, and a negative sample flips it.
Zero makes no arrow. Negative flips it.
Spin once, and the scaled arrows all lean right, so they add up. The total is four.
Right speed: they all lean right and add.
Now spin twice as fast.
Now spin twice instead.
This time the arrows loop round and cancel out, so the total is zero.
The arrows loop back and cancel.
Run the test at every spin speed, zero to seven.
Run the test at every spin speed.
Each test reads all eight samples, and its answer grows one orange bar.
Each test reads all 8 samples.
Eight tests give eight bars. Together they are the D F T.
Eight tests give eight bars.
Eight tests times eight samples is sixty-four products.
That is 8 × 8 = 64 products.
For a real wave, the bars come as a mirror pair.
A real wave gives a mirror pair.
Sample a seven hertz wave eight times a second.
Take 8 samples in one second.
But the dots fit a one hertz wave just as well.
The dots fit a 1 Hz wave too.
Half the sample rate, four hertz, is the limit.
Half the sample rate is the limit.
So the seven hertz wave folds back, and shows up as one hertz.
So 7 Hz folds back onto 1 Hz.
The cure is to sample faster than twice the wave. Then the bar stays at seven.
Sample faster than twice the wave.
The D F T treats the window as if it repeated for ever.
The DFT repeats the window.
Whole cycles join smoothly, so there is one clean bar.
Whole cycles join: one clean bar.
Add half a cycle, and the ends no longer meet.
Half a cycle more: the ends do not meet.
The jump needs many frequencies to describe it, so the energy leaks into other bars.
The jump needs many frequencies: the bars leak.
A smooth fade at both ends, called a Hann window, shrinks the leak.
A smooth fade at both ends shrinks the leak.
A recording has a hum mixed through it. The D F T turns it into bars.
The DFT turns the wiggle into bars.
The hum is just one pair of bars.
The hum is one pair of bars.
Delete both of them, the hum's bar and its mirror.
Delete both bars.
Then go back with the inverse D F T. The hum is gone, and the slow wave is untouched.
Go back: the hum fades away.
A direct D F T of eight samples does sixty-four products.
A full DFT does all 64 products.
Now split the samples into evens and odds.
Split into even and odd samples.
Each half size D F T costs sixteen products.
Two half-size DFTs cost 16 each.
A butterfly joins an even and an odd answer, using one product for two answers.
One butterfly: one product, two answers.
Thirty-two products for the halves, plus four for the butterflies, makes thirty-six, not sixty-four.
32 plus 4 is 36 products, not 64.
Each half is a D F T too, so split it again.
Each half is a DFT too: split again.
Keep going until single samples remain. Each is its own D F T.
Down to single samples.
Then butterflies combine pairs, one level at a time, climbing back up.
Butterflies combine pairs, level by level.
Three levels of four butterflies makes twelve.
Three levels of four: 12 butterflies.
The result is the same eight bars as the direct D F T.
The same answer as the direct DFT.
For a million samples, the direct way takes eighteen minutes.
Direct: 18 minutes for a million samples.
The F F T takes just point zero two seconds.
The FFT: 0.02 seconds.
That is about fifty thousand times less work.
About 50,000 times less work.
Any repeating signal is a sum of sine waves.
The D F T tests every frequency, and gives bars.
The F F T keeps halving the problem, and does far less work.
